scope: Only the replay process submitting thread, inside exactly joined steady VTDecodeCall intervals. No unrelated process data or raw stack/address dump is included.

raw_syscall_export.hash_note: Full raw export hashed after all timing runs completed.

capture.process_identity: Exact submit timestamp matches between signpost payloads and CSV

methodology: Streamed the syscall XML with ElementTree.iterparse, resolving typed global XML id/ref values and clearing each row after filtering; did not construct a full document tree.

Selected the submitting TID determined by exact CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW submit timestamp joins between replay CSV and VTDecodeCall signposts. Filtered out all other threads and processes before saving the local subset.
Used the 480 frames marked steady by scripts/analyze-vt-profile.py after the 120 offered warmup frames; each call interval is in the trace time domain.

Intersected each selected syscall start/end with each steady VTDecodeCall interval on the same thread. All selected syscall intervals were wholly contained, so their wall durations require no clipping or attribution to inter-frame sleep.
Classified synchronous XPC only when the exported stack explicitly contained xpc_connection_send_message_with_reply_sync. Deeper unsymbolized frames were not inferred.
Per-frame percentiles include zero overlap on frames without that syscall. Each share divides summed syscall wall overlap by summed trace-native submit-call wall time, not by submit-to-callback time.
interpretation: The largest selected syscall interval is a condition-variable wait: exactly one psynch_cvwait per steady call, via _pthread_cond_wait.

The next largest syscall family is Mach IPC, dominated by explicitly synchronous XPC send/reply paths. Both execute within the public VT submit call, before its output callback and before Qt wrapping.
This identifies API-visible waiting and IPC overhead; it does not establish what the condition variable or remote service is waiting for, nor isolate hardware decode execution.
limitations: This is a single instrumented HEVC SDR8 4K60 diagnostic, not an uninstrumented performance comparison or proof of the same breakdown for AV1/HDR/other hardware.

Use vt-profile-analysis.json thread-state intersections for Running/Blocked/Runnable accounting. Raw syscall cputime/waittime annotations were observed not to partition syscall wall duration consistently and are deliberately omitted here.
Signpost emission adds instrumentation overhead. Trace-native interval endpoints bracket the API but differ slightly from raw timestamp endpoints; the joined profile evidence quantifies those deltas.
Middle framework and application frames in the all-process syscall export lack symbol/binary metadata. This report names only visible symbols and does not infer missing callers.
Synchronous XPC spans are a subset of mach_msg2 spans, not an additional disjoint cost. Per-phase percentiles are not additive.
The raw all-process export stays local; this portable artifact contains only target-specific aggregate evidence.
